question: What can Forge World implement directly, without creating a parallel incompatible architecture?

findings.note: Forge world identity is sha256 over a canonical semantic projection. No new codec.
Forge actions are wrapped into ActionDescriptors by the adapter; actionKey stays the identity.
Prime recommendations over Forge worlds replay through the existing verifier unchanged.
Forge implements all eight required methods. It is an ordinary adapter, not a special case.
Forge is self-contained and binds no external root, so it needs no environment binding of its own. It inherits the discipline, not the variable.
Replay records use the same self-excluding hash rule: a document may not contain its own hash.
Forge binds records to (scenarioSeed, worldHash, configHash) instead of a live session id, because there is no live session.
Forge observations carry canonicalState and observationHistory in exactly the shapes the normalizer accepts.
Prime runs against Forge with no Forge-specific branch anywhere in its path.
Forge has eleven relation types; the adapter projects them onto the three Nexus kinds. The projection is declared in the contract table, not buried in the adapter.
Forge channels are authoritative world state and are emitted as frames directly.
Forge OutcomePackets carry a scalar plus a component vector, which is the shape the validator already requires.

newContractsIntroduced: FORGE_REWARD_V1 — a versioned reward vector, which no existing contract provided
FORGE_REPLAY_V1 — a training record, which no existing contract provided
the semantic admission gate — a discipline inherited from Stage 2L.23, now generalized to scenario generation
conclusion: Forge World implements the existing Adapter SDK contract directly. Sentinel needs no change to run against it, and Forge needs no decision path of its own.
